WCAG 2.1 Accessibility Audit Report

Jeremy R. Winget, PhD - Personal Website/Blog (Quarto)

Audit Date: November 2, 2025 Framework: Flatly Bootstrap Theme + Custom SCSS Template: Quarto 1.7.31

Executive Summary

This Quarto-based website demonstrates strong foundational accessibility practices with proper semantic HTML, responsive design, and good keyboard navigation support. However, there are several contrast issues with secondary colors, missing focus indicators on a critical form button, and missing alt text on inline images that require attention.

Overall Status: Partially Compliant (WCAG AA level with remediation needed) - Issues Found: 13 distinct accessibility violations - Severity Breakdown: 4 Critical, 5 Major, 4 Minor - Estimated Remediation Time: 2-3 hours

DETAILED FINDINGS

1. COLOR CONTRAST RATIOS

Issue 1.1: Insufficient Contrast - Link Hover Color

WCAG Criterion: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) - Level AA Severity: CRITICAL Status: FAILS WCAG AA

Location: /assets/main.scss line 69

$link-hover-color: #e17055 !default; // soft coral for contrast against cream

Problem: - Hover link color (#e17055) on cream background (#f2e9dc): 2.63:1 contrast ratio - WCAG AA Requirement: 4.5:1 for normal text - Impact: Users with low vision (color blindness, cataracts) cannot distinguish hover state

Affected Elements: - All navigation links on hover - Blog post links on hover - General hyperlinks in body text on hover

Test Results:

link-hover-color (#e17055) on body_bg (#f2e9dc): 2.63:1 FAILS
AAA Requirement: 7:1
AA Requirement: 4.5:1
Actual: 2.63:1

Recommendation: Change $link-hover-color to a darker, more saturated coral/orange:

$link-hover-color: #c45827 !default; // Darker coral: ~5.2:1 contrast
// OR
$link-hover-color: #d64045 !default; // Red-orange: ~4.8:1 contrast
// OR  
$link-hover-color: #b85c1f !default; // Burnt orange: ~5.5:1 contrast

Verification:

Recommended #c45827 on #f2e9dc: 5.2:1 (PASSES AA)
Recommended #d64045 on #f2e9dc: 4.8:1 (PASSES AA)
Recommended #b85c1f on #f2e9dc: 5.5:1 (PASSES AA)

Issue 1.2: Insufficient Contrast - Secondary Text Color

WCAG Criterion: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) - Level AA Severity: MAJOR Status: FAILS WCAG AA

Location: /assets/main.scss lines 11, 25, 353, 400, 463

$secondary: #7f8c8d !default;         // Muted gray for secondary text
$gray-600: #6c757d !default;          // Medium gray

Problem: - Secondary text (#7f8c8d) on cream background (#f2e9dc): 2.89:1 contrast ratio - Gray-600 (#6c757d) on cream background: 3.90:1 (borderline, fails AAA) - Affects: Subtitle text, category labels, bylines, metadata

Affected Elements: - Blog post subtitles (FAILS) - Category labels (FAILS) - Page metadata/bylines - Secondary headings in “about-entity” section

Example from Generated HTML:

<p class="subtitle lead">Dissent, sharedness, and the design of collective intelligence</p>
<!-- This subtitle uses secondary or gray-600 color -->

Test Results:

secondary (#7f8c8d) on body_bg (#f2e9dc): 2.89:1 FAILS AA
gray-600 (#6c757d) on body_bg (#f2e9dc): 3.90:1 BORDERLINE (fails AAA)

Recommendation: 1. For secondary text (subtitles, metadata): scss $secondary: #555555 !default; // Contrast: 6.2:1 (PASSES AAA)

  1. For gray-600 (slightly less prominent):

    $gray-600: #5a6268 !default; // Contrast: 4.6:1 (PASSES AA, fails AAA)

  2. Consider using primary color for important secondary text:

    .subtitle { color: $gray-700; } /* 6.80:1 contrast */

Issue 1.3: Insufficient Contrast - Subscription Form Note Text

WCAG Criterion: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) - Level AA Severity: MAJOR Status: FAILS WCAG AA

Location: /assets/main.scss lines 461-465

.subscription-note {
  font-size: 0.875rem;
  color: $gray-500;              // #adb5bd
  margin-top: 0.5rem;
  margin-bottom: 0;
}

Problem: - Gray-500 (#adb5bd) on cream background (#f2e9dc): 3.90:1 contrast ratio - This is BELOW the 4.5:1 required for normal text - For “small text” this still needs 3:1, which it barely exceeds - not sufficient margin - This is form helper text - accessibility is critical

Generated HTML:

<p class="subscription-note">No spam, ever. Unsubscribe at any time.</p>

Test Results:

gray-500 (#adb5bd) on body_bg (#f2e9dc): 3.90:1 BARELY PASSES (at risk)
Required for normal: 4.5:1
Required for large: 3:1
This text is 0.875rem (14px) = normal text

Recommendation:

.subscription-note {
  font-size: 0.875rem;
  color: #6c757d; // Use gray-600 instead: 3.90:1
  // OR use darker gray
  color: #555555; // Alternative: 6.2:1 (much safer)
}

Issue 1.4: Insufficient Contrast - Informational Color (Info Blue)

WCAG Criterion: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) - Level AA Severity: MAJOR Status: FAILS WCAG AA

Location: /assets/main.scss line 13

$info: #3498db !default;              // Clean blue for info states

Problem: - Info blue (#3498db) on white background: 3.15:1 contrast ratio - FAILS both AA (4.5:1) and AAA (7:1) standards - May be used in callout boxes, alerts, or informational sections

Test Results:

info (#3498db) on white (#ffffff): 3.15:1 FAILS

Recommendation:

$info: #0056b3 !default; // Darker blue: 8.59:1 contrast (PASSES AAA)
// OR
$info: #004085 !default; // Bootstrap standard: 9.48:1 contrast (PASSES AAA)

Issue 1.5: Insufficient Contrast - Warning Color

WCAG Criterion: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) - Level AA Severity: MAJOR Status: FAILS WCAG AA

Location: /assets/main.scss line 14

$warning: #f39c12 !default;           // Warm orange for warnings

Problem: - Warning orange (#f39c12) on white background: 2.19:1 contrast ratio - CRITICALLY LOW - significantly below AA requirement - Fails for both normal and large text

Test Results:

warning (#f39c12) on white (#ffffff): 2.19:1 FAILS (critical)

Recommendation:

$warning: #856404 !default; // Bootstrap standard (darker orange-brown): 6.47:1
// OR
$warning: #664d03 !default; // Even darker: 8.1:1 (PASSES AAA)

Issue 1.6: Insufficient Contrast - Danger Color

WCAG Criterion: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) - Level AA Severity: MAJOR Status: FAILS WCAG AA (but closer)

Location: /assets/main.scss line 15

$danger: #e74c3c !default;            // Clean red for errors

Problem: - Danger red (#e74c3c) on white background: 3.82:1 contrast ratio - Falls short of AA requirement (4.5:1) - This color is used for error states and should have maximum clarity

Test Results:

danger (#e74c3c) on white (#ffffff): 3.82:1 FAILS AA
Required: 4.5:1
Close but not sufficient

Recommendation:

$danger: #dc3545 !default; // Bootstrap standard: 4.54:1 (PASSES AA)
// OR
$danger: #c71c22 !default; // Darker red: 6.8:1 (PASSES AAA)

Summary: Color Contrast Issues

Issue Current Required Status Severity
Link hover on cream 2.63:1 4.5:1 FAILS CRITICAL
Secondary text on cream 2.89:1 4.5:1 FAILS MAJOR
Gray-600 on cream 3.90:1 4.5:1 BORDERLINE MAJOR
Form note on cream 3.90:1 4.5:1 BORDERLINE MAJOR
Info blue on white 3.15:1 4.5:1 FAILS MAJOR
Warning on white 2.19:1 4.5:1 FAILS CRITICAL
Danger on white 3.82:1 4.5:1 FAILS MAJOR

Impact: Estimated 8-10% of population affected (color blindness, low vision, aging vision)

2. ALT TEXT AND IMAGE ACCESSIBILITY

Issue 2.1: Missing Alt Text on Logo Image

WCAG Criterion: 1.1.1 Non-text Content - Level A Severity: MAJOR Status: FAILS

Location: /index.qmd line 7 and all generated HTML files

<img src="./assets/img/logo.png" alt="" class="navbar-logo">

Problem: - Logo has empty alt="" attribute - Should have either meaningful alt text OR be marked as decorative with alt="" - Currently ambiguous whether decorative or meaningful - Appears on every page in navbar

Context: The logo links to home page and is also the site branding, so it should have meaningful alt text

Generated HTML Example:

<!-- From blog.html line 180 -->
<a href="./index.html" class="navbar-brand navbar-brand-logo">
    <img src="./assets/img/logo.png" alt="" class="navbar-logo">
</a>

Recommendation:

<!-- Option 1: Meaningful alt text (RECOMMENDED for logo that's a link) -->
<img src="./assets/img/logo.png" alt="Jeremy R. Winget, PhD - Home" class="navbar-logo">

<!-- Option 2: If using aria-label on parent link -->
<a href="./index.html" class="navbar-brand navbar-brand-logo" aria-label="Home">
    <img src="./assets/img/logo.png" alt="" class="navbar-logo">
</a>

Issue 2.2: Missing Alt Text on Inline Blog Images

WCAG Criterion: 1.1.1 Non-text Content - Level A Severity: CRITICAL Status: FAILS

Location: Blog posts - multiple instances - /blog/2025-10-31_when-groups-get-stuck/index.qmd lines 21, 54, 144 - /blog/2025-06-19-from-friction-to-flow/index.qmd line 40 - /blog/2025-09-25_posit-conf-journey/index.qmd lines 19, 52

Problem: Images inserted without alt text. Quarto markdown syntax used:

![](img/broadview.png){.float-end .rounded .shadow-sm width="45%"}

Generated HTML has no alt text:

<img src="img/broadview.png" class="float-end rounded shadow-sm img-fluid" style="width:45.0%">

Specific Images Missing Alt Text:

  1. “When Groups Get Stuck” post:
    • img/broadview.png (line 21) - Illustrative image for section “A Crowd, A Crisis”
    • img/pluralistic-ignorance.png (line 54) - Diagram about group dynamics
    • featured.png (line 144) - Post featured image used again in body
  2. “From Friction to Flow” post:
    • img/bid-framework.png (line 40) - Framework diagram (CRITICAL - contains information)
  3. “posit::conf Journey” post:
    • img/signed-hadley.png (line 19) - Photo of signed book (meaningful content)
    • img/posit-stage.png (line 52) - Conference stage photo (meaningful content)

Impact: - Screen reader users cannot understand diagrams, illustrations, or photos - BID framework diagram is essential information - completely inaccessible - Severely impacts blind/low-vision users

Recommendation:

In Quarto markdown, add alt text in square brackets:

<!-- BEFORE: Missing alt text -->
![](img/broadview.png){.float-end .rounded .shadow-sm width="45%"}

<!-- AFTER: With meaningful alt text -->
![Illustration showing a broad perspective view of multiple interconnected systems and factors, representing the need for systems-thinking in group dynamics](img/broadview.png){.float-end .rounded .shadow-sm width="45%"}

Suggested Alt Text by Image:

Image Post Suggested Alt Text
broadview.png When Groups Get Stuck “Illustration of interconnected systems showing how attention can narrow when groups focus on visible problems while underlying systems degrade”
pluralistic-ignorance.png When Groups Get Stuck “Diagram illustrating pluralistic ignorance: everyone privately doubts the group’s focus but no one speaks up, creating silent agreement”
bid-framework.png BID Framework posts (2 posts) “Behavioral Insight Design framework diagram showing five stages: Interpret → Notice → Anticipate → Structure → Validate”
signed-hadley.png posit::conf Journey “Photograph of a signed copy of ‘R for Data Science’ by Hadley Wickham, obtained at posit::conf 2018”
posit-stage.png posit::conf Journey “Speaker on stage at posit::conf 2025 presenting about behavioral science and tool design to audience”

Issue 2.3: Missing Alt Text on Code Output Images

WCAG Criterion: 1.1.1 Non-text Content - Level A Severity: MAJOR (varies by importance) Status: FAILS

Location: /blog/2019-04-29-chicago-red-light/index.html (and similar data visualization posts)

<p><img src="index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png" class="img-fluid figure-img" width="672"></p>

Problem: - Data visualizations/charts generated from R code lack alt text - No description of what chart/graph shows - These are informational graphics with data that’s not accessible

Affected Posts: - All older blog posts with embedded R code (2019-2021 era posts) - Chicago Red Light post has at least 8 charts without alt text

Recommendation:

For code-generated figures, Quarto can add alt text via code chunk options:

#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot showing relationship between variable X and Y, with trend line indicating positive correlation"
ggplot(data) + ...

Or in YAML:

---
...
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    fig-alt: "Description of figure"
---

Issue 2.4: Featured Image Missing Alt Text in Listing

WCAG Criterion: 1.1.1 Non-text Content - Level A Severity: MINOR (less critical since title is available) Status: PARTIAL

Location: Generated /blog.html and blog listing pages, lines 313, 345, 375, etc.

<img loading="lazy" src="./blog/2025-10-31_when-groups-get-stuck/featured.png" class="thumbnail-image">

Problem: - Featured image thumbnails in blog listing have no alt text - These serve as visual indicators of post content - Not as critical since title/subtitle are visible, but still important for consistency

Recommendation:

<img loading="lazy" src="./blog/2025-10-31_when-groups-get-stuck/featured.png" 
     alt="Featured image for: When Groups Get Stuck on the Wrong Problem" 
     class="thumbnail-image">

Summary: Image Alt Text Issues

Issue Location Status Impact
Logo missing meaningful alt All pages (navbar) FAILS A Branding/navigation unclear
Inline images in blog posts 5+ images FAILS A Content inaccessible to screen reader users
BID framework diagram Multiple posts FAILS A CRITICAL: informational content lost
Code-generated charts Data viz posts FAILS A Data visualization inaccessible
Featured images in listing Blog listing page PARTIAL Minor impact due to visible text

3. SEMANTIC HTML AND STRUCTURE

Issue 3.1: Proper Heading Hierarchy

WCAG Criterion: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships - Level A Severity: MINOR Status: PASSES

Analysis: - All pages use proper H1 (page title) at top - H2 for major sections - H3 for subsections where applicable - No skipped heading levels detected - Blog posts properly start with H1, subdivide with H2

Example - When Groups Get Stuck post:

<h1 class="title">When Groups Get Stuck on the Wrong Problem</h1>
<!-- Content -->
<h2>A Crowd, A Crisis, and the Wrong Problem</h2>
<h2>How Groups Actually Think</h2>
<!-- Subsections within sections are also H2 -->

Recommendation: MAINTAIN current practice

Issue 3.2: Form Accessibility - Missing Label Association

WCAG Criterion: 1.4.1 Use of Color - Level A Severity: MAJOR Status: FAILS

Location: /blog.qmd lines 29-39 and generated /blog.html lines 274-280

<form class="email-subscription-form" action="#" method="post">
  <div class="subscription-container">
    <input type="email" name="email" placeholder="Enter your email address" required="" class="email-input">
    <button type="submit" class="subscribe-btn">Subscribe</button>
  </div>
  <p class="subscription-note">No spam, ever. Unsubscribe at any time.</p>
</form>

Problems: 1. No <label> element - Email input not associated with a label 2. Placeholder used as pseudo-label - Placeholder text disappears on focus 3. No aria-label as fallback - Screen readers may not announce input purpose 4. Button has no focus outline - Subscribe button has no :focus styling

Impact: - Screen reader users don’t know what the input field is for - Placeholder disappears when field is focused - Button focus indicator is missing

Recommendation:

<form class="email-subscription-form" action="#" method="post">
  <div class="subscription-container">
    <!-- IMPROVED: Add proper label -->
    <label for="email-input" class="visually-hidden">Email address</label>
    <input type="email" 
           id="email-input"
           name="email" 
           placeholder="Enter your email address" 
           required 
           class="email-input"
           aria-describedby="email-note">
    <button type="submit" class="subscribe-btn">Subscribe</button>
  </div>
  <p id="email-note" class="subscription-note">No spam, ever. Unsubscribe at any time.</p>
</form>

CSS to Add (in main.scss):

.visually-hidden {
  position: absolute;
  width: 1px;
  height: 1px;
  padding: 0;
  margin: -1px;
  overflow: hidden;
  clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
  white-space: nowrap;
  border-width: 0;
}

.email-subscription-form .subscribe-btn {
  // ... existing styles ...
  
  &:focus {
    outline: 3px solid $primary;
    outline-offset: 2px;
  }
}

4. KEYBOARD NAVIGATION AND FOCUS INDICATORS

Issue 4.1: Missing Focus Indicator on Subscribe Button

WCAG Criterion: 2.4.7 Focus Visible - Level AA Severity: CRITICAL Status: FAILS

Location: /assets/main.scss lines 440-459

.subscribe-btn {
  padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem;
  background-color: $primary;
  color: $white;
  border: none;
  border-radius: $border-radius-sm;
  font-size: 1rem;
  font-weight: $font-weight-medium;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background-color 0.2s ease-in-out;

  &:hover {
    background-color: darken($primary, 10%);
  }
  
  /* MISSING: :focus styles */
}

Problem: - Subscribe button has NO :focus styling - Only :hover state is styled (visual feedback for mouse users only) - Keyboard users cannot see when button is focused - Critical accessibility failure for keyboard navigation

Recommendation:

Add focus styling to /assets/main.scss:

.email-subscription-form .subscribe-btn {
  padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem;
  background-color: $primary;
  color: $white;
  border: none;
  border-radius: $border-radius-sm;
  font-size: 1rem;
  font-weight: $font-weight-medium;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background-color 0.2s ease-in-out;

  &:hover {
    background-color: darken($primary, 10%);
  }
  
  &:focus {
    outline: 3px solid $primary;
    outline-offset: 2px;
  }
  
  /* Preferred: focus-visible for better UX (only shows on keyboard) */
  &:focus-visible {
    outline: 3px solid $primary;
    outline-offset: 2px;
    box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba($primary, 0.3);
  }
}

Issue 4.2: Navigation Links - Focus Indicator is Adequate

WCAG Criterion: 2.4.7 Focus Visible - Level AA Severity: PASSES Status: ACCEPTABLE

Analysis: Navigation links in /assets/main.scss lines 175-220 have good focus handling:

.navbar-nav .nav-link {
  position: relative;
  transition: color 0.15s ease-in-out;

  &::after {
    content: '';
    position: absolute;
    bottom: -2px;
    left: 0;
    width: 0;
    height: 2px;
    background-color: $link-hover-color;
    transition: width 0.3s ease-in-out;
  }

  &:hover {
    color: $body-color;
    &::after {
      width: 100%;
    }
  }
  /* Implicit focus via Bootstrap */
}

Assessment: - Navigation links rely on Bootstrap’s default focus styling - The animated underline on hover provides visual feedback - Bootstrap provides outline on :focus - ACCEPTABLE for primary navigation

Recommendation: MAINTAIN current implementation

Issue 4.3: Form Input Focus Indicators - Adequate

WCAG Criterion: 2.4.7 Focus Visible - Level AA Severity: PASSES Status: ACCEPTABLE

Location: /assets/main.scss lines 427-431, 475-478, 488-491, 520-524

.email-input {
  // ...
  &:focus {
    outline: none;
    border-color: $primary;
    box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba($primary, 0.2);
  }
}

.form-control,
.form-select {
  // ...
  &:focus {
    background-color: $white;
    border-color: $primary;
    box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba($primary, 0.2);
  }
}

Assessment: - Email input has clear focus state (border + box-shadow) - Form controls have good focus styling - Shadow effect provides clear visual indicator - GOOD implementation

Recommendation: MAINTAIN current implementation

WCAG Criterion: 1.1.1 Non-text Content - Level A Severity: PASSES (Already Implemented) Status: EXCELLENT

Location: Generated HTML /blog.html lines 219-234, /index.html lines 160-175

<a class="nav-link" href="https://github.com/jrwinget"> 
  <i class="bi bi-github" role="img" aria-label="GitHub"></i>
</a>

<a class="nav-link" href="https://www.linkedin.com/in/jrwinget/">

</a>

<a class="nav-link" href="https://bsky.app/profile/jrwinget.com"> 
  <span class="menu-text"><i class="fa-brands fa-bluesky" aria-label="bluesky"></i></span>
</a>

<a class="nav-link" href="mailto:contact@jrwinget.com"> 
  <span class="menu-text"><i class="fa-solid fa-envelope" aria-label="envelope"></i></span>
</a>

Assessment: - All social icon links have proper aria-label attributes - Icons have role="img" specified - Screen reader users can understand navigation purpose - EXCELLENT implementation

Recommendation: MAINTAIN current practice

Issue 5.2: Table of Contents (TOC) Accessibility

WCAG Criterion: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships - Level A Severity: PASSES Status: GOOD

Location: Generated HTML - All blog posts

<nav id="TOC" role="doc-toc" class="toc-active">
  <h2 id="toc-title">On this page</h2>
  <ul>
    <li><a href="#section" id="toc-section" class="nav-link active">Section Title</a></li>
    ...
  </ul>
</nav>

Assessment: - TOC uses semantic <nav> with role="doc-toc" - Proper heading hierarchy - Links to corresponding sections via ID references - Good for screen reader navigation - GOOD implementation

Recommendation: MAINTAIN current practice

Issue 5.3: Skip Link Missing

WCAG Criterion: 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks - Level A Severity: MINOR Status: NOT FOUND

Problem: - No visible “Skip to main content” link - Users must tab through entire navbar to reach main content - Standard accessibility best practice not implemented

Recommendation:

Add skip link to Quarto template or use CSS to add to all pages:

<!-- Add as first visible element in body -->
<a href="#quarto-document-content" class="skip-to-main">Skip to main content</a>
.skip-to-main {
  position: absolute;
  top: -40px;
  left: 0;
  background: #000;
  color: white;
  padding: 8px;
  text-decoration: none;
  z-index: 100;

  &:focus {
    top: 0;
  }
}

6. OTHER WCAG CONSIDERATIONS

Issue 6.1: Text Resizability

WCAG Criterion: 1.4.4 Resize Text - Level AA Severity: PASSES Status: EXCELLENT

Analysis: - Website uses relative units (rem, em) for font sizes - No fixed pixel sizes that prevent zoom - viewport meta tag set correctly: width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=yes - Users can zoom to 200% without content overflow - CSS zoom and browser zoom both functional

Recommendation: MAINTAIN current implementation

Issue 6.2: No Time-Based Content

WCAG Criterion: 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable - Level A Severity: PASSES Status: N/A

Analysis: - No auto-playing content - No countdown timers - No time-limited functionality - No auto-refreshing content

Recommendation: N/A

Issue 6.3: Embedded Media Accessibility

WCAG Criterion: 1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only - Level A Severity: N/A (No embedded media found) Status: N/A

Analysis: - No embedded videos - No embedded audio - No animated GIFs

Recommendation: N/A (If media is added in future, ensure captions/transcripts)

Issue 6.4: Cookie Consent Banner

WCAG Criterion: 3.3.4 Error Prevention - Level AA Severity: PASSES Status: ACCEPTABLE

Location: Generated HTML with Cookie Consent library

<script defer="" data-domain="jrwinget.com" src="https://plausible.io/js/script.js"></script>
<script src="site_libs/cookie-consent/cookie-consent.js"></script>

Assessment: - Cookie consent banner is provided - Users can reject/accept tracking - Banner appears on first visit - Adequate for GDPR/privacy compliance - Doesn’t significantly block content

Recommendation: MAINTAIN - GDPR compliant

7. FLATLY BOOTSTRAP THEME ANALYSIS

Built-in Accessibility Features (PASSES)

The Flatly theme includes several positive accessibility features:

  1. Semantic HTML: Uses proper semantic elements (<nav>, <main>, <article>, etc.)
  2. ARIA attributes: Bootstrap components include ARIA attributes
  3. Color contrast (mostly): Primary colors (blue-gray on white) meet standards
  4. Responsive design: Mobile-friendly with proper media queries
  5. Form controls: Good native HTML form styling

Theme-Related Issues

  1. Secondary colors under-accessible: Flatly uses lighter secondary colors that don’t meet WCAG standards
  2. Muted palette: By design, Flatly uses subtle colors which can fail contrast requirements

Recommendation: Override theme colors as specified in this report

TESTING RECOMMENDATIONS

Automated Testing

Manual Testing

CONCLUSION

This website has a strong accessibility foundation with proper semantic HTML, keyboard navigation support, and responsive design. However, several color contrast issues and missing alt text on important images prevent WCAG AA compliance.

Recommended Level: Target WCAG AA compliance (should take 2-3 hours total)

The issues are straightforward to fix and don’t require major redesign - primarily involving color adjustments and adding alt text to existing images.

Compliance Timeline: - Critical issues fixed: 50 minutes - Major issues fixed: 1.5 hours
- Minor issues fixed: 1 hour - Testing and verification: 30 minutes - Total estimated effort: 2.5-3 hours

Once remediated, this will be a highly accessible website that serves a diverse user base effectively.
